question: Should outbound message sends keep the shared 10-second gateway default and opt into a longer bound at the relevant send caller, or should every defaulted outbound gateway caller move to 75 seconds?
rationale: The incident supports waiting beyond Telegram's bounded provider send, but the PR changes a shared default without establishing that the longer failure latency is intended for all current callers.

options.title: Scope the longer timeout
options.body: Keep the shared default unchanged and pass a timeout above the provider bound only from outbound message-send paths that need it.

options.title: Adopt 75 seconds globally
options.body: Accept the longer default after auditing all current callers and documenting the intentional failure-latency change.

options.title: Drop the timeout change
options.body: Make no timeout adjustment if current-main delivery behavior has made the original 10-second ambiguity obsolete.

recommendation.title: Scope the longer timeout
recommendation.body: Keep the shared default unchanged and pass a timeout above the provider bound only from outbound message-send paths that need it.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the most relevant recent Telegram transient-recovery implementation and can connect the provider bound to the current delivery path, though core outbound ownership may be shared.
